title: Private VPC fleet projections and purchase plan Q2-2026
content:
Purpose:
This working doc captures a near-term procurement plan and capacity projection for Private/VPC customer deployments (3–36 month horizon). It is a pragmatic mix of spreadsheet-style calculations, BOM line items, and assumptions so Solutions/Procurement can start RFQs and SRE/PE can review rack/network constraints.

High-level summary: 
- Target: support 5 large enterprise private customers (multi-region), plus a standing template for self-hosted single-tenant racks.
- Time window: purchases staged over H2-2026 with a pilot buy in Q3 and larger replenishment in Q4.
- Primary workload profile: mixed chat + embeddings + reranking; tail latency SLO 200ms p95 for small models and 1s p95 for 70B-ish models.
- Safety factor: target 25% spare GPU capacity for failover and rolling upgrades.

Assumptions (inputs):
- Models and baseline per-request token cost: small (2.7B) ~0.5k tokens per request average, medium (7B) 1.2k tokens, large (70B) 5k tokens.
- Typical inference latency per token (single-GPU, optimized kernel, no kv-cache warm): small=0.7ms/token, medium=1.2ms/token, large=4.0ms/token.
- Batch efficiencies: continuous batching yields 1.6x throughput improvement at 64-token average and 4x at 256 tokens for medium/large depending on kernel. Conservative multiplier used: 1.8x for planning.
- Target util: 70% average sustained GPU utilization (to keep headroom for tail SLOs)
- Cost amortization window: 3-year useful life for procurement CAPEX calculations

Mapping of model classes to GPU types (for capacity estimate):
- Small models (2–4B): L4 / A10G (recommended: cost-optimized L4 for embeddings-heavy workloads)
- Medium models (7–13B): A10G / A100-40GB (preferred A10G for cost, A100 if memory needed)
- Large models (30–70B): H100-80GB or A100-80GB (H100 preferred if throughput matters)

Key variables (spreadsheet inputs):
- QPS_region: expected requests per second for region (string list in sheet)
- Avg_tokens_per_request
- Avg_tokens_per_second_per_gpu = GPU_throughput_tokens_per_second * batch_multiplier * gpu_count
- Desired_p95_latency
- Safety_factor (1.25)

Example per-region projection (text table):
Region: us-west1
- Expected peak QPS: 120
- Traffic mix: 50% small, 35% medium, 15% large
- Effective tokens/sec (peak) = (120 * ((0.5*500) + (0.35*1200) + (0.15*5000))) = 120 * (250 + 420 + 750) = 120 * 1420 = 170,400 tokens/sec
- Representative GPU throughput (tokens/sec) assuming medium config on H100 = 60,000 tokens/sec (after batching multiplier of 1.8 applied to single-request baseline)
- Raw GPUs required = ceil(170,400 / 60,000) = 3
- With 70% util headroom: provision GPUs = ceil(3 / 0.7) = 5
- Apply 25% spare capacity = 5 * 1.25 ≈ 7 GPUs for us-west1

Region: eu-west1
- Expected peak QPS: 60
- Traffic mix: 40% small, 40% medium, 20% large
- Effective tokens/sec = 60 * ((0.4*500)+(0.4*1200)+(0.2*5000)) = 60*(200+480+1000)=60*1680=100,800 tokens/sec
- GPUs required (H100 60k tps) = ceil(100,800 / 60,000) = 2
- Provisioned with util & spare = ceil(2 / 0.7 * 1.25) = ceil(3.57) = 4 GPUs

Region: ap-southeast1 (pilot)
- Expected peak QPS: 30
- Effective tokens/sec approx = 30 * 1420 = 42,600 tokens/sec (pilot mix)
- GPUs required = ceil(42,600 / 60,000) = 1
- Provisioned with util/spare = ceil(1 / 0.7 * 1.25) = ceil(1.79) = 2 GPUs

Consolidated short-term fleet (pilot + initial enterprise):
- us-west1: 7 H100 GPUs
- eu-west1: 4 H100 GPUs
- ap-southeast1: 2 H100 GPUs
- Buffer pool (for staging/overprovision across racks): 6 A10G GPUs (cheaper, used for small/medium offload and dev)
- Total GPUs (initial buy): 19 GPUs (13 H100 + 6 A10G)

BOM (line-item style, unit cost estimates for RFQ prep):
- H100-80GB SXM server (1U/2U chassis with PCIe adapter option) – unit: GPU card only or integrated node price used. Estimated unit price (card) = $25,000. Full 2U node with 4x H100 + CPU + NVMe + NIC + PSU ~ $160,000
- A10G GPU card (PCIe) – unit price = $4,500. Node with 4x A10G ~ $28,000
- 2U node components (per node): CPU (dual 32c) $6,000, 2x 32GB DDR5 $1,200, 2x 4TB NVMe (OEM) $2,000, 200G NIC $2,500, chassis + PSUs + rails $4,000
- Rack & PDUs: per rack cost (42U populated) estimate $6,000 (non-recurring)
- Top-of-Rack switch (2 x 100/200G ports) + spares per rack $18,000
- Rack power distribution and breakers (install) $3,500
- Network optics (QSFP) per link $800
- Cables, rails, misc $1,200
- KMS/HSM appliance (if customer needs on-prem keys) $12,000
- 3-year enterprise support (hardware + expedited RMAs) ~ 8% of HW list price/year → used as multiplier 0.24 of HW cost over 3 years

Procurement math examples (simplified):
- If buying 4x H100 per node (typical density): one 4x H100 node cost ≈ $160k → per-GPU allocated cost = $40k (node-level amortization)
- If we need 13 H100 GPUs total → 4x nodes: 4 nodes * $160k = $640k (covers 16 GPUs)
- A10G nodes: 6 GPUs bought as 1.5 nodes ⇒ buy 2 nodes (2 * $28k = $56k) to cover 6 cards (with spare slots)
- Rack count estimate: assume 4x H100 nodes = 4 * 2U = 8U, with network + storage + buffer probably fits 1 rack; overhead: planning to put nodes across 2 racks for redundancy per region. So for us-west1 (target 7 H100 GPUs -> 2 nodes) allocate 1 rack; eu-west1 (4 GPUs -> 1 node) -> 1 rack; ap-southeast1 (2 GPUs -> partial node) -> collocate with buffer/dev -> 1 rack. Anticipate 3 racks initial across three regions + 1 central staging rack = 4 racks. Rack CapEx (HW+network) ~ ($160k * 4 nodes + A10G nodes) + rack/network ~ approx $900k ballpark (very conservative).

Operational costs (high level, per year):
- Power and colocation: assume $1.20 per watt per year all-in (including facility, PUE, power management). Rough per-node power: 4x H100 node typical TDP + overhead ~ 6.5kW → yearly ~ 6,500 * 1.2 = $7,800 per node/year.
- Network egress: variable by customer contract, propose to budget $18k/year per region as initial placeholder.
- Support & spares: 3-year support = 24% of HW list price (multiplied in CAPEX schedule or OPEX depending on contract).

Risk / sensitivity notes (to include in RFQ/PO):
- GPU market price volatility: H100 list and availability can swing – include CLAs for lead time and price protection.
- Lead time: expect 8–20 weeks for H100 procurement; plan pilot nodes earlier.
- Power & racks: confirm colo power availability and breaker reservation with sites before PO.
- Cooling and rack density: confirm per-rack heat removal capability; some sites require water cooling or derating.

Deliverables for next week (owner assigned):
- Procurement: draft RFQ for H100 nodes + A10G options (owner: Mariana Silva)
- SRE/PE: validate per-rack thermal and breaker plans for us-west1 colo (owner: Ravi Menon)
- Solutions Eng: finalize region-level QPS inputs for pipeline customers (owner: Asha Patel)
- Finance: produce 3-year TCO variant table (CAPEX-first vs managed-support OPEX) (owner: Joel Chen)

Open questions / TODOs:
- Should we prefer denser 8-GPU nodes (4U) vs 4x in 2U nodes for thermal/cost tradeoffs? (SRE input required)
- Confirm whether customers require HSM on-prem or can use cloud KMS (security impact to BOM)
- Evaluate leasing/consumption services vs CAPEX for customers who want pay-as-you-go

Appendix: quick calculation snippets (copyable into a sheet):
- tokens_per_sec = QPS * avg_tokens_per_request
- gpu_throughput_tps = baseline_tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * batch_multiplier
- raw_gpus = ceil(tokens_per_sec / gpu_throughput_tps)
- provisioned_gpus = ceil(raw_gpus / target_utilization * safety_factor)
- nodes_needed = ceil(provisioned_gpus / gpus_per_node)
- amortized_hw_per_gpu = (node_total_price / gpus_per_node) / (years_amortized)

Notes on variability: keep a small pool of A10G for prewarm and low-cost embedding tasks to reduce H100 usage; consider an autoscaler policy that prioritizes small-model traffic onto A10G nodes when possible to reduce marginal cost.

This is intentionally a working, somewhat messy planning doc. I expect updates as we get RFQ responses and better per-customer QPS. Save an updated sheet export to the Drive folder and tag JIRA-ENGPD-1987 for tracking.

End of doc.
